title: A Java process started a reconnaissance tool or a shell running one
detail: A Java process (java.exe, javaw.exe, or VMware Horizon's Tomcat service ws_TomcatService.exe) was the direct parent of a Windows tool that reports on the account, the host or the domain, of a built-in binary that downloads or runs code, or of a command shell or PowerShell whose command line does one of these (process.parent_name, process.name, process.command_line).
impact: Java application servers (Jenkins, Jira, Confluence, Keycloak, Spring Boot applications) serve requests; they do not ask which account they run as. An exploited Java application - Log4Shell, Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a deserialization or template-injection flaw - runs the attacker's first commands this way, with the service's account.
focus: Read the command line and the account. Find which application the Java process was: its own command line (-jar, the class path, the install folder) names it. Read that application's access log at that minute for the request that caused it and the client's address, list what else the same Java process started, and check its Java version against the vendor's advisories.

running_process.focus: It is running now. Read its command line and account, and the Java parent's command line (-jar, the class path, the install folder) for the application. Before stopping anything, record what the Java process has started and its network connections, then read that application's access log for the request that caused it.

notes: High, not critical: a Java program may legitimately run one of these tools, for example a build job that calls whoami directly. Build servers (Jenkins, Gradle) start cmd.exe from java.exe for every build step, so a shell is matched only when its own command line does reconnaissance, a download or an encoded command. Left out because Java libraries and desktop programs call them for benign reasons: ipconfig, getmac, wmic, tasklist, reg (hardware and network details) and rundll32 (java.awt.Desktop opens links with it). Covers only the parent names listed: a Java service under another renamed launcher is not seen (Tomcat's own service names are WEB-SERVER-STARTED-PROCESS's). An exploit that never starts a process is not seen. Not tagged T1190: a process tree does not show how the Java process was made to do this. Module Executions, not Webshells: the Webshells module keeps only processes whose parent is one of its own web servers, so a rule there never sees java.exe. Proven end to end 2026-11-18 on Windows 11 with Security 4688 and Sysmon 1.

tests.note: a Jenkins build step: a shell with no reconnaissance in its command line
a shell from Java with no command line recorded: unknown, never a signal
a Java library reading the network adapters for a hardware ID
a Java desktop program opening a link in the browser
whoami typed in a command prompt
a parent whose name only ends like java.exe
a program whose name only ends like whoami.exe
